excerpt: Compare furnished and unfurnished Dubai rental investments using collected rent, furnishing costs, tenant fit and ongoing owner expenses.
introduction:
Furnishing a Dubai rental can change the tenants a home attracts and the rent it may achieve, but the extra revenue must be weighed against furniture, replacement, management and vacancy costs. Compare the actual apartment over your intended holding period rather than assuming furnished always earns a better return.

This guide focuses on an owner's long-term rental decision. The calculation uses example figures to show how furnishing and operating costs affect rental income.
takeaways: Compare collected rent after vacancy and owner costs, including furniture purchase and replacement.
Use an agreed inventory and clear repair, damage and deposit terms for supplied items.
Check whether the intended lease is long-term or a permitted holiday home; their obligations differ.

sections.heading: What changes when the owner furnishes?
sections.body:
A furnished offer may include beds, seating, dining furniture, appliances, curtains and kitchen equipment, but the actual list must be agreed. A partly furnished home can have a different cost and tenant appeal. Prepare an inventory with the condition of each item and clarify who maintains or replaces it.

Compare recent signed leases for similar apartments in the same building with the same parking, condition and included services. Record whether each is furnished and what that means in the lease. Compare advertised rents with signed leases and the time taken to let similar homes.

The [Business Bay and Dubai Marina area guide](/journal/business-bay-vs-dubai-marina-rental-investment) provides location context, while the exact building and tenant determine the relevant comparison.

sections.heading: Compare first-year cash
sections.body:
Assume a sample furnished option collects AED 96,000 after vacancy, has AED 20,000 owner operating costs and requires AED 12,000 of furniture in the first year. The remaining cash before finance and tax is AED 64,000. A sample unfurnished option collects AED 87,000 after vacancy and has AED 18,000 of owner costs, leaving AED 69,000.

The furnished unit collects more rent but produces less first-year cash in this example because of setup costs. The chart shows those sample results. The example compares how furnishing and operating costs affect the two rental strategies.

For later years, do not charge the full initial furniture purchase again, but budget for wear, replacement, storage and the value recovered when the furniture is sold. A cash-flow calculation and accounting depreciation are different measures.

sections.heading: Evaluate the full holding period
sections.body:
Estimate furniture purchase, delivery, installation, replacement and removal over the years you expect to own the apartment. Compare the additional collected rent after vacancy with those costs. If the home will be sold furnished, be conservative about the value a buyer will pay for used items.

Run a shorter holding-period scenario. A large initial outlay may be harder to recover if the tenant leaves early or you sell sooner than planned. Also test a lower rent premium and a major appliance replacement.

Include the unit's building service charges, management, repairs and insurance in both cases. DLD's [service charge index](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/eservices/service-charge-index/) helps check approved community charges; request the statement and area basis for the exact unit.

sections.heading: Agree the lease and inventory
sections.body:
List every included item, its condition and any serial number where useful. Take dated photographs with the tenant and agree how faults should be reported, who will arrange repairs and how damage and normal wear will be assessed. Confirm the deposit and return process in the written lease.

DLD's [tenancy registration service](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/eservices/register-renew-ejari-contract/) describes registering or renewing a contract through Ejari. Check the current process and fees, and verify the landlord's or representative's authority.

If you appoint a manager, agree the fee basis, inspection schedule, repair approval limits and reporting. Avoid assuming an annual management quote includes furniture replacement or a new tenant placement fee.

sections.heading: Distinguish long-term and holiday-home use
sections.body:
A furnished long-term lease is not automatically a holiday-home operation. If considering short stays, verify DET registration, the unit permit and current building rules before operating. Cleaning, utilities, guest support and seasonal occupancy can produce a very different cost structure.

The [short-term versus long-term rental guide](/journal/how-to-compare-short-term-and-long-term-rental-income-in-dubai) explains how to compare those strategies on the same annual basis. Do not compare a nightly gross rate directly with annual net rent.

For either strategy, check insurance, lender restrictions and the agreement with any operator. Compare the advertised rent with furnishing, service charges and maintenance to assess net income.

sections.heading: Estimate the rent premium needed
sections.body:
As a simple starting point, divide the expected net cost of furniture by the years you intend to use it. If a sample AED 12,000 setup has no resale value and lasts three years, the cost is AED 4,000 per year before replacement, financing and the timing of payments. The furnished home would need at least that much additional annual net income to cover this narrow cost.

Add delivery, repairs, replacement and any extra vacancy or management charge before drawing a conclusion. If you expect resale proceeds, test a case where they are lower or zero. Keep the actual upfront cash requirement separate from the annual comparison.

sections.heading: Assess a current property
sections.body:
Browse the [Aliyas Dubai project collection](/projects?emirate=Dubai) and [contact Aliyas](/contact) with the apartment, budget and intended lease. Ask for current building charges and comparable lease evidence, then calculate both options using the specific unit's terms. Record the dates and sources of those figures so the comparison can be updated when the lease or costs change.

Keep a reserve for vacancy and repairs and verify the applicable official requirements before letting.
